basis: Defining congenital heart defects and profound intellectual disability; minor facial and digital anomalies do not establish additional functional organ damage.
Congenital absence of the opening from the left ventricle into the aorta.
Larval infection; destructive CNS larva migrans occurs in over 30% of recognized clinical cases. Ocular and visceral injury are less consistently common.
Inherited deficient globin synthesis causes anemia; skeletal changes and iron-related organ injury do not characterize most patients across this umbrella.
Inborn serine biosynthesis deficiency defined by microcephaly, neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures.
Hip dislocation and joint laxity define the syndrome; cardiac septal/valvular defects and hearing abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Urinary abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Named constellation comprises a cerebellar malformation, a nasopharyngeal tumor and a congenital defect of the diaphragm, a skeletal muscle.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with universal developmental delay and intellectual disability; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Germinoma arising in the central nervous system; endocrine and visual damage depend on tumor location and are not established as common across this adult umbrella.
Inherited neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; weakness and ptosis reflect impaired neuromuscular transmission. Respiratory insufficiency occurs in only 5-29%.
Defining gingival fibromatosis and nail/terminal-phalangeal hypoplasia; intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%. Hepatosplenomegaly occurs in only 5-29%.
Erosive oral lichen planus is an immune-mediated disease causing destructive inflammation of oral mucosa; cutaneous involvement is not required.
Neurological movement syndrome typically associated with third-ventricular cysts and hydrocephalus.
Inherited deficiency of marrow megakaryocytes causes thrombocytopenia and may progress to broader marrow failure.
The defining constellation combines rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia and scoliosis with retinal degeneration.
Skeletal dysplasia with joint laxity and dislocations; laryngotracheomalacia occurs in 5/8 patients and laryngeal stenosis in 30-79%, establishing common airway pathology.
Chronic inflammation of labial minor salivary glands and lip mucosa. Carcinoma is a separate disease; nonspecific immune annotations do not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Broad umbrella of destructive skin and mucosal ulceration, predominantly cutaneous and gastrointestinal forms; corneal involvement belongs to a site-specific minority.
Acrofacial skeletal dysplasia with defining dental and ectodermal abnormalities; oligodontia occurs in 80-99% and sparse hair in 30-79%. Intelligence is normal.
Louse-transmitted relapsing bacterial infection; thrombocytopenia affects most clinical cases, often with anemia. Organomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by a chromosomal deletion; malignant myeloid cells occupy marrow and blood.
Congenital loss of intestinal-wall collagen impairs bowel motility; the enteric nervous system is normal or near-normal, so no additional neurological axis.
Vaginal disease affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; infection is only one subtype and does not define this umbrella.
Inherited primary adrenal glucocorticoid deficiency; renal salt wasting and hypoglycemic coma occur in only 5-29%, without established common renal or neurological damage.
Inherited type 2 diabetes susceptibility subtype; retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy and vascular complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
